title: How Many Ranges Are Not Inside Another Range?

concept.title: Sort by start, and for equal starts put the longer range first
body: A range `(a, b)` is **covered** by a range `(c, d)` if `c <= a` and `b <= d`: it lies completely inside the other one. After removing all the covered ranges, how many ranges remain? For `(1, 4) (3, 6) (2, 8)` the range `(3, 6)` is covered by `(2, 8)`, so 2 remain. For `(1, 2) (1, 4) (3, 4)` the range `(1, 4)` covers the other two: 1 remains. All the ranges are different.

Sort the ranges by the **start, increasing**, and for equal starts by the **end, decreasing**. Now every range that could cover the current one comes **before** it in the list: a range that covers it has a smaller start, or the same start and a larger end (which is why the longer one goes first when the starts are equal). While walking through the sorted list, keep `max_end`, the **largest end among the ranges before**. The current range is covered exactly when its end is **at most `max_end`**. Otherwise it is not covered: count it and update `max_end`.

body.code:
ranges.sort(key=lambda r: (r[0], -r[1]))
count = 0
max_end = -1
for start, end in ranges:
    if end > max_end:               # nothing before covers it
        count += 1
        max_end = end
print(count)

body: The tie-break on equal starts matters: with the ends in increasing order the shorter range would be counted as not covered before its longer partner was seen. After the sort the work is one pass: O(n log n) in total. This is the shape of many *domination* problems: sort by one key, break ties in the right way, and scan with the best value of the other key.

statement: `n` different closed ranges are given. A range is covered if some other range contains it completely: `other.start <= start` and `end <= other.end`. Print the number of ranges that are not covered by any other range.
inputFormat: The first line has `n`: the number of ranges.
Each of the next `n` lines has two numbers `start` and `end`: a closed range from `start` to `end`.
outputFormat: Print the number of ranges that are not covered.
hints: Sort by start increasing and, for equal starts, by end decreasing.
Keep the largest end seen so far.
A range whose end is not larger than that is covered.

starter.python:
import sys
input = sys.stdin.readline

n = int(input())
ranges = [list(map(int, input().split())) for _ in range(n)]

# Your code here

explanation: The ranges are sorted by start increasing and, for equal starts, by end decreasing; scanning them with the largest end seen so far, a range is covered exactly when its end is at most that value, otherwise it is counted.
solution.complexity: Time O(n log n), space O(n).

code.python:
import sys
input = sys.stdin.readline

n = int(input())
ranges = [list(map(int, input().split())) for _ in range(n)]

ranges.sort(key=lambda r0: (r0[0], -r0[1]))
count = 0
max_end = -1
for start, end in ranges:
    if end > max_end:
        count += 1
        max_end = end
print(count)
